title: The Donkey and the Turban
summary: An illiterate peasant brought an unreadable, scribbled letter to Nasruddin: "Mulla, you wear the grand turban of a scholar; read this letter for me!"...
full_text:
An illiterate peasant brought an unreadable, scribbled letter to Nasruddin: "Mulla, you wear the grand turban of a scholar; read this letter for me!"

Nasruddin examined the handwriting; it was an illegible scrawl from a foreign merchant. "My good man," sighed Nasruddin, "this handwriting is so terrible that no mortal can decipher it."

The peasant became angry: "Shame on you! You wear a turban the size of a watermelon, yet you cannot read a simple letter!"

Nasruddin took off his enormous turban, placed it upon the peasant's head, and said: "Here! Now that you are wearing the watermelon turban, read the letter yourself!"
moral: A magnificent turban does not grant the ability to read what is written in gibberish.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Donkey and the Turban"?
options: Foolishness hides wisdom; laughter teaches truth
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
